key_variances.final_explanation: **acct_1 changed by −53.2% (−879 BYN), driven by "Loan given" dropping −969 BYN (992 → 23), with 1 contributor (tag_1) accounting for 100% of that change — mainly the non-recurrence of October's single 854 BYN loan.** A new 299 BYN "Clothes" charge (also tag_1) partially offset the decline.

acct_3 fell 66.1% (251 → 85 BYN) on a broad-based pullback led by Gifts (-60 BYN, to zero — three one-off purchases of 30/15/15 BYN in October simply didn't recur) and Cafe (-56 BYN, -60.2%, the statistically unusual mover by zscore, with November reduced to small 3-8 BYN tickets). Both categories are 100% concentrated in tag_1 with no offsetting contributors, as is all of this account's spend.

acct_1 income fell 56.4% (-1676 BYN), driven mainly by Debt return / Borrowed money dropping -1321 BYN (-96.4%), a single tag_5 contributor accounting for 100% of that change with no offsetting contributors — essentially the absence of October's one-off 1345 BYN repayment, replaced by just 49 BYN in November. A secondary drag was Second work (-284 BYN, 100% from tag `2th_work`), partly offset by Job (+119 BYN); note the debt category's materiality rests on robust_ratio with only 5 periods of history, so it's large but not statistically confirmed as unusual.

notes.note: In acct_1, "Loan given" is 100% tag_1 and is lumpy/episodic rather than recurring: monthly totals are dominated by occasional single large disbursements (e.g. one 854 BYN transaction in 2025-10 out of 992 BYN total). Month-over-month swings in this category should be read as timing of one-off loans, not a change in run-rate spending.

acct_3 spending is entirely tagged tag_1 across all categories (Gifts, Cafe, Leisure, Food), so it behaves like a single-owner personal account — tag-level concentration analysis will always return 100% on tag_1 and adds no discriminating power. Use category- or transaction-level drilldowns instead. Gifts is episodic/lumpy (one-off 15-30 BYN purchases, zero in some months, only 4 periods of history so moves score via robust_ratio), while Cafe is a recurring small-ticket stream (3-8 BYN transactions) with enough history for zscore.

In acct_1, this category is entirely tag_5 and is lumpy/non-recurring: it consists of occasional large one-off repayments (e.g. a single 1345.00 BYN item on 2025-10-20) on top of small ~25-50 BYN items. Month-over-month swings here are driven by presence/absence of a single large transaction rather than a run-rate change, and it has thin history (n=5, materiality flagged via robust_ratio not zscore). Treat spikes in this category as timing noise unless a large item recurs.
